assets.description: Close daylight photograph of the three surviving columns of the Temple of Castor and Pollux in the Roman Forum. All three Corinthian capitals are visibly articulated: acanthus leaves, volutes and abaci can be inspected. The fluted shafts, weathered stone, joints and cracks, architrave and surviving entablature fill the frame. The columns are light against a blue sky, not silhouettes. The lower shafts continue beyond the source framing; the bases and podium are not shown. The photographer identifies this specific image as Temple of Castor and Pollux 3705. The source watermark and black caption/signature strip remain intact.
